examples.en: The old paper is curled up into a roll.
The marble rolled far away across the floor.

examples.ko: 얇은 김이 도르르 말려서 먹기 힘들어요.
examples.en: The thin seaweed sheet curls up, so it is hard to eat.

examples.ko: 아이가 이불을 도르르 말고 누워 있어요.
examples.en: The child is lying there rolled up in the blanket.
The toilet paper unrolled and piled up on the floor.

examples.ko: 동전이 책상 아래로 도르르 굴러 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: The coin rolled off and fell under the desk.

explain: 작고 가벼운 것이 굴러가거나 종이처럼 얇은 것이 말리는 모양에 써요. '데굴데굴'은 좀 더 크게 구르는 느낌이라 도르르와 느낌이 달라요. 주로 '도르르 말리다', '도르르 구르다'로 써요.
explain_en: It describes small, light things rolling along or thin things like paper curling up. '데굴데굴' feels bigger and heavier, so the feeling is different. It is mostly used as '도르르 말리다' or '도르르 구르다'.

examples.ko: 불이 나가서 방이 완전히 암흑이 됐어요.
examples.en: The power went out and the room became pitch dark.
It's pitch dark inside the cave, so you need a flashlight.

examples.ko: 전쟁 때는 암흑 같은 시간을 보냈다고 해요.
examples.en: They say people lived through dark times during the war.
That movie begins in darkness.
Everything went pitch black before my eyes.
The whole city was plunged into darkness by the blackout.

explain: 암흑은 빛이 전혀 없는 어둠이에요. '어둠'보다 더 짙고, '암흑기'처럼 힘든 시대를 말할 때도 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '깜깜하다'를 더 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 그 나라는 긴 암흑기를 지나 다시 일어났어요.
phrases.en: That country rose again after a long dark age.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a long period of hardship without hope.

explain_en: 암흑 is darkness with no light at all, deeper than 어둠. It also describes hard times, as in 암흑기 (dark age). In daily talk people say 깜깜하다 more often.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 얼굴이 우락부락해서 처음엔 무서웠어요.
examples.en: His face looked so tough that I was scared at first.

examples.ko: 우락부락한 팔뚝의 아저씨가 짐을 들어 줬어요.
examples.en: A man with thick, rough-looking arms carried my bags.
He looks tough, but he likes puppies.
My older brother worked out and his body became beefy.
The tough-looking guard greeted me first.
His voice is rough too, so the children are afraid of him.

explain: 생김새나 체격이 거칠고 억세 보일 때 써요. 외모를 평가하는 말이라 앞에서 직접 말하면 실례일 수 있어요. '우락부락하게 생겼지만 착하다'처럼 겉모습과 다르다고 말할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: It describes a face or build that looks rough and tough. Since it comments on appearance, saying it to someone's face can be rude. It is often used to contrast looks with personality, as in '우락부락하게 생겼지만 착하다'.

examples.en: My grandfather has dignity even without speaking.
The king entered with a majestic stride.

examples.ko: 사자는 위엄 있는 모습으로 서 있어요.
examples.en: The lion stands with a majestic look.

examples.ko: 새 교장 선생님은 위엄을 지키려고 노력해요.
examples.en: The new principal tries to keep an air of authority.
You can feel a sense of grandeur from that old building.
I practiced speaking with authority.

explain: '위엄'은 사람이나 대상에서 느껴지는, 함부로 대하기 어려운 무게감이에요. '위엄 있다', '위엄을 지키다'처럼 써요. '권위'와 비슷하지만 '위엄'은 겉모습이나 태도에서 느껴지는 힘에 더 가까워요.
explain_en: '위엄' is the weight a person or thing carries that makes it hard to treat lightly. Use it as '위엄 있다' or '위엄을 지키다'. Close to '권위', but '위엄' leans toward the power felt in appearance and manner.

examples.en: It was such a tempting offer that I thought about it for a moment.

examples.ko: 빵집에서 나는 유혹적인 냄새를 그냥 지나칠 수 없었어요.
examples.en: I couldn't just walk past the tempting smell coming from the bakery.

examples.ko: 광고 속 모델의 표정이 너무 유혹적이에요.
examples.en: The model's expression in the ad is so enticing.

examples.ko: 밤늦게 먹는 라면은 유혹적인 음식이지만 건강에는 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Ramen late at night is a tempting food, but it's bad for your health.
Be careful not to fall for that enticing way of talking.

examples.ko: 친구가 보낸 유혹적인 여행 계획에 마음이 흔들려요.
examples.en: My friend's tempting travel plan is making me waver.

explain: '매력적'은 그냥 마음이 끌린다는 좋은 느낌이고, '유혹적'은 넘어갈 것 같아서 조금 조심해야 하는 느낌이 있어요. 보통 '유혹적인 제안', '유혹적인 냄새'처럼 명사 앞에서 '-인'을 붙여 써요.
explain_en: '매력적' just means attractive in a good way, while '유혹적' carries a feeling that you might give in, so you should be a little careful. It is usually used before a noun with '-인', as in '유혹적인 제안' or '유혹적인 냄새'.

en: desolate and silent; lonely and still

examples.en: The dawn street was so quiet it felt desolate.

examples.ko: 이사 가고 나니 집이 적막해서 허전해요.
examples.en: After moving, the house is so silent that it feels empty.

examples.ko: 겨울 바다는 사람이 없어 적막한 느낌이에요.
examples.en: The winter sea has no people, so it feels desolate and still.
On nights that feel too silent, I play music.
After the children left, the school became desolately quiet.
I heard the temple in the mountains is hushed even in the daytime.

explain: '조용하다'가 소리가 적다는 뜻이라면, '적막하다'는 거기에 쓸쓸하고 외로운 느낌이 더해져요. 일상 대화보다는 글이나 이야기에서 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: While '조용하다' simply means there is little noise, '적막하다' adds a lonely, desolate feeling. It sounds more natural in writing or storytelling than in everyday conversation.

examples.en: The negotiations have been dragging on for months.
The construction is so slow that the residents are angry.
Everyone is worn out because of the sluggish meeting.
I don't know why the project is so sluggish.

examples.ko: 일이 지지부진하게 진행되면 팀 분위기도 나빠져요.
examples.en: When work proceeds sluggishly, the team's mood gets worse too.
The matter that had been dragging on was finally resolved.

explain: 그냥 '느리다'가 아니라 일이 잘 나아가지 않고 답답하게 늘어진다는 느낌이에요. 주로 협상, 공사, 논의, 수사처럼 일의 진행에 쓰고 '지지부진한 ~'의 형태로 뉴스에서 자주 들어요.
explain_en: It is not just 'slow' but carries the frustrating feeling that something is not moving forward and keeps dragging. It is mostly used for how a matter progresses, such as negotiations, construction, discussions and investigations, and you often hear it as '지지부진한 ~' in the news.

en: clear and pure (of a voice or sound)

examples.ko: 그 가수는 청아한 목소리로 노래를 불러요.
examples.en: That singer sings in a clear, pure voice.
The bell of the mountain temple rang out clear and pure.

examples.ko: 목소리가 청아해서 아나운서 같다는 말을 들었어요.
examples.en: I was told I sound like an announcer because my voice is clear and pure.

examples.ko: 청아하고 맑은 피리 소리에 마음이 편해졌어요.
examples.en: The clear, pure sound of the flute put my mind at ease.

examples.ko: 그 아이의 웃음소리는 청아하다고 할 만해요.
examples.en: That child's laughter can be called clear and pure.

examples.ko: 청아하지만 힘 있는 목소리가 극장에 퍼졌어요.
examples.en: A voice that was clear yet strong spread through the theater.

explain: 소리, 특히 목소리·새소리·종소리가 맑고 깨끗할 때 써요. '맑다'는 물·하늘·소리에 다 쓰지만, 청아하다는 귀로 듣는 소리에 주로 써요. 글에서 칭찬하는 말이고, 일상 대화에서는 '목소리가 맑아요'라고 해요.
explain_en: It describes sound, especially voices, birdsong and bells, that is clear and clean. '맑다' is used for water, sky and sound, but '청아하다' is mostly for sounds the ear hears. It is a complimentary word used in writing, while in daily talk people say '목소리가 맑아요'.

examples.en: Even after seeing his exam results, he stayed calm.
How can you say that so casually?
I was shocked that he lied with such a straight face.
I tried to stay composed even in a crisis.
How can you be so unruffled?

examples.ko: 발표 전에는 태연해 보여도 속으로 많이 떨려요.
examples.en: Before a presentation I may look calm, but inside I'm very nervous.

explain: '침착하다'는 당황하지 않고 차분하게 행동하는 좋은 느낌이 있고, '태연하다'는 놀라거나 미안해할 만한 일에도 아무렇지 않은 듯한 모습을 말해요. 그래서 때로는 '뻔뻔하다'는 비판이 섞이기도 해요. '태연하게', '태연히'로 자주 써요.
explain_en: '침착하다' has a positive feel of staying composed and acting calmly, while '태연하다' describes looking unbothered even about something that should surprise or embarrass you. So it can carry a hint of criticism, like being shameless. It is often used as '태연하게' or '태연히'.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 얼굴이 험상궂어서 처음엔 무서웠어요.
examples.en: He has a menacing face, so I was scared at first.

examples.ko: 생김새는 험상궂지만 알고 보면 아주 다정해요.
examples.en: He looks tough, but once you know him he's very kind.
Why are you scowling so fiercely?

examples.ko: 험상궂어 보이는 개가 사실은 아주 얌전해요.
examples.en: The dog that looks fierce is actually very gentle.
He stared at me with a menacing expression, and I was startled.
The man who looked so rough seemed gentle when he smiled.

explain: 주로 얼굴이나 표정이 사납고 무섭게 생긴 것을 말해요. 일상에서는 '무섭게 생기다'라고도 하고, '험상궂게 생기다', '인상을 험상궂게 쓰다'처럼 써요. 사람 앞에서 외모를 이렇게 말하면 실례가 될 수 있어요.
explain_en: It describes a face or expression that looks fierce and scary. In daily talk people also say '무섭게 생기다', and it appears as '험상궂게 생기다' or '인상을 험상궂게 쓰다'. Saying it about someone's looks to their face can be rude.

examples.ko: 열심히 준비했는데 시험이 취소돼서 헛고생만 했어요.
examples.en: I prepared hard, but the exam was canceled, so it was all for nothing.

examples.ko: 괜히 먼 길을 갔다가 헛고생을 했어요.
examples.en: I went all that way for no reason and wasted my effort.

examples.ko: 이렇게 하면 헛고생이 될 테니 방법을 바꿔요.
examples.en: If we do it this way it'll be wasted effort, so let's change the method.

examples.ko: 헛고생이라고 생각했지만 그 경험이 도움이 됐어요.
examples.en: I thought it was a waste of effort, but the experience turned out to help.

examples.ko: 헛고생을 하지 않으려면 미리 전화해 보세요.
examples.en: To avoid a wasted trip, call ahead first.
The shop was closed, so we went through all that trouble for nothing.

explain: 고생을 했는데 아무 보람이 없었을 때 써요. 비슷한 '헛수고'는 애쓴 일이 소용없다는 뜻이 크고, '헛걸음'은 갔는데 보람 없이 돌아온 경우에 써요. 보통 '헛고생을 하다', '헛고생만 하다'로 말해요.
explain_en: Use it when you went through hardship and got nothing for it. Similar '헛수고' stresses that the effort was useless, and '헛걸음' fits a trip that ended with nothing gained. It is usually said as '헛고생을 하다' or '헛고생만 하다'.
